title: Radical Candor
prompt:
Act as a leadership communication coach using Kim Scott's Radical Candor framework.
Situation  : [DESCRIBE THE PERSON, THE PERFORMANCE ISSUE, AND WHAT YOU HAVE  
                     SAID OR AVOIDED SO FAR]
Step 1: Diagnose which quadrant I am currently in:
Radical Candor (high care + high challenge)
Ruinous Empathy (high care + low challenge)
Obnoxious Aggression (low care + high challenge)
Manipulative Insincerity (low on both)
Step 2: Write the Radical Candor version of this conversation  what I should actually say.
Step 3: Write the Ruinous Empathy version the version I am probably tempted to give.
Step 4: Give me 2 opening lines that demonstrate both care and directness simultaneously.
Radical Candor Matrix
Radical Candor
Top right quadrant
High Care, High Challenge
High Care, Low
Ruinous Empathy
Challenge
Bottom right quadrant
Low Care, High
Challenge
Obnoxious Aggression
Top left quadrant
Low Care, Low
Challenge
Manipulative Insincerity
Bottom left quadrant
PRO TIP
Ruinous Empathy is the most harmful leadership style precisely because it feels kind.
When you protect someone from honest feedback, you protect yourself from an
uncomfortable conversation and deny them the information they need to grow. The
person who needs the feedback most is the one whose manager feels worst about giving it.
